significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that deceptive generation has a "linearly decodable signature in intermediate activations" whose cross-topic and cross-elicitation discrimination exceeds output-based lie detection; this is primarily form (i), an existence claim, supplemented by a comparative performance regularity rather than a causal mechanism. It would establish a useful phenomenon and constrain detector choice across contexts, but it would not explain how deception is computed or caused; work such as MacDiarmid et al.'s Simple Probes Can Catch Sleeper Agents and Pacchiardi et al.'s black-box lie detection makes the claimed reliability boundary operationally relevant. The negative branch would rule out a broadly transferable linear internal detector under these notions of belief and deception, but not nonlinear signatures or naturally emergent deception, so the true and false states are distinguishable yet limited. In the topic-substitution check, generic LLM safety and interpretability would not earn this score, while the specific cross-context internal-versus-output detector comparison does; nevertheless, latent-state probing is close to the competent default hypothesis for this topic.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "linear probe over intermediate activations" serving as an internal lie detector, with the substantive promise that it "generalizes across topics and elicitation methods better than output-based lie detection." Because activations are taken "at the point of assertion," the handle is concurrent or post hoc rather than a clearly ex-ante forecast, although auditors could potentially use it to gate outputs during deployment. Its claimed relation transfers across tasks and elicitation contexts, but no cross-model or cross-architecture regularity is asserted, so after moving to a new model the signature may have to be rediscovered rather than yielding a predicted quantity; downstream users nevertheless include model auditors and deployers, not only deception researchers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: broad mechanistic safety alone supplies no reusable handle, whereas the specific cross-context probe and comparison with black-box detection support moderately above-median reach.
